headline: VALHALLA METALS SUN 26-006 RIPS 32.6M @ 4.35% CuEq IN ALASKA — Best 2026 Hole Also Hits 6.5m @ 6.98%; Two More Intervals Above 5% Pending
snippet: Valhalla Metals (TSXV: VMXX) released the first assay results from its 2026 drill program at the Sun Project in Alaska's Ambler Mining District: hole Sun 26-006 returned 32.6 metres at 4.35% copper-equivalent including a 6.5-metre core grading 6.98% CuEq. Two further holes — 11.2m @ 5.67% and 12.5m @ 3.97% — round out the initial batch, with three holes still pending. The Sun VMS system sits in the same Ambler district where the Pentagon recently took a 10% equity stake in Trilogy Metals, underscoring Washington's strategic interest in this copper-cobalt-germanium corridor.

headline: AYA GOLD & SILVER DRILLS 239 G/T AGEQ OVER 17M AT BOUMADINE — Peak Interval Hits 953 g/t Over 1.7m; Company Adds 3 New Exploration Permits
snippet: Aya Gold & Silver (TSX: AYA) reported a drill hole at its Boumadine Project in Morocco returning 239 g/t silver-equivalent over 17.0 metres, with a high-grade 1.7-metre core grading 953 g/t AgEq. The company simultaneously received three new exploration permits, extending the project's footprint. Boumadine has emerged as one of the world's highest-grade undeveloped silver-gold projects; today's results confirm grade continuity at depth and add to a growing permit estate that sets the stage for an expanded resource estimate.

headline: KAZATOMPROM Q3 OUTPUT SURGES 12% TO 7,216 TU — Spot Uranium Peaked $90.10/lb in Quarter; Full-Year Guidance Held at 27,500–29,000t
snippet: Kazatomprom (LON: KAP), the world's largest uranium producer, reported Q3 2026 attributable output of 3,915 tU — up 16% year-on-year — with 100%-basis production of 7,216 tU rising 12%. For the nine months through September, attributable output is 10,969 tU, also up 12%. The average realized price was $81.50/lb while spot uranium peaked at $90.10/lb in Q3; full-year production guidance is maintained at 27,500–29,000 tU. Rising output from the world's largest producer alongside firm spot prices reinforces the uranium bull thesis heading into what analysts expect will be a tight 2027 market.

headline: CHINA'S RARE EARTH EXPORT TRUCE EXPIRES NOVEMBER 10 — No Extension Announced; Three Scenarios Could Reshape Western Supply Chain Within Days
snippet: China's Ministry of Commerce suspension of its October 2025 rare-earth export control expansion expires on November 10, 2026, with no formal extension announced as of November 4. The measures cover seven medium and heavy rare earths — including dysprosium and yttrium critical for defence magnets — and analysts outline three scenarios: full extension, selective reactivation targeting specific end-uses, or complete restoration of the October 2025 controls. Western manufacturers face a parallel US rule restricting Chinese-origin magnet materials in defence procurement, effective January 1, 2027.

headline: NUCLEAR PLANT BUILDS AT 40-YEAR HIGH — Structural Demand Signal That Uranium Spot at $89/lb Has Yet to Fully Price In
snippet: Global nuclear plant construction has reached its highest level in four decades, with over 70 reactors currently under build worldwide. The build-out is concentrated in Asia — China, India, and South Korea lead the pipeline — while the US and UK have announced fresh reactor programmes for net-zero and energy security. With long-lead fuel procurement cycles meaning reactors under construction today will drive uranium demand for decades, analysts argue current spot prices of around $89/lb still materially underprice the structural demand now being locked in.

headline: GOLD NEAR $3,960 AND SILVER BACK ABOVE $51 — GoldSeek Analysis: Oversold Extremes Ask 'Is the Worst Over?' After Six-Week Silver Slide
snippet: After gold hit a one-year low and silver posted six consecutive weekly declines through $49, a GoldSeek analysis finds both metals at oversold extremes with momentum indicators consistent with a bottoming process. Gold has stabilized near $3,960 and silver has bounced back above $51; with both metals trading 60–70% below their 2026 peaks, the piece argues that mean-reversion forces are building — though the Fed's December meeting remains the decisive catalyst for whether a recovery holds.

headline: SILVER'S SIXTH STRAIGHT DEFICIT YEAR — New Tech Demand in Nanoparticles and Fuel Cells Builds an Industrial Floor Under the Metal's Price
snippet: Money Metals profiles an expanding set of industrial applications for silver that extend beyond solar: cheaper silver nanoparticle production for printed electronics and 5G networks, and silver-catalyst hydrogen fuel cells. ETP silver holdings have fallen by 60 million ounces in 2026 as metal moves from vaults into industrial use. With the Silver Institute projecting a sixth consecutive structural market deficit, the piece argues the industrial demand floor under $50 silver is firmer than current sentiment suggests.

headline: GOLD-SILVER RATIO WIDENS TO 78.8 — Historically One of the Best Entry Signals for Silver; Metal Has Averaged 50% Gains Over 12 Months From These Levels
snippet: A GoldSeek analysis flags the gold-silver ratio at 78.8 — up from around 68 three months ago — as an unusually stretched reading historically associated with significant silver outperformance over the following 12 months. Silver's current price near $50, its structural six-year supply deficit, and the ratio's mean-reversion tendency combine for a setup that veteran precious metals analysts call one of the best risk/reward situations for silver in a generation. Silver ETP holdings fell 60 million ounces this year while industrial demand grew, tightening visible supply.

headline: COPPERCORP DRILLS 12.0M @ 0.54% CU AT JUKES, TASMANIA — Tasmanian Government Backs Phase 2 with A$100k EDGI Co-Funding Grant
snippet: CopperCorp Resources (TSXV: CPER) released final assay results from its Jukes Cu-Au prospect in Tasmania, highlighted by a 12.0-metre interval grading 0.54% copper, 0.14 g/t gold, and 0.89 g/t silver. The company simultaneously received an A$100,000 Exploration Drilling Grant Initiative co-funding award from the Tasmanian government to fund a Phase 2 deep diamond hole in an area inaccessible to current equipment. Government grant support is a meaningful de-risking signal for a junior with tight capital: it validates the geological target and partially offsets the cost of a high-capital deep hole.

headline: GDX FREE CASH FLOW/EV AT RECORD HIGH — Analyst Calls Historic Buy on Miners as Forward P/E Hits 5-Year Low Despite Gold's Best Year Since 1979
snippet: A GoldSeek analysis makes the valuation case for the VanEck Gold Miners ETF (GDX) after a 20%+ correction from its 2026 peak: free cash flow to enterprise value is at a record high, forward P/E multiples are at five-year lows, and EV/EBITDA has compressed to below historical averages — all while gold is on track for its best year since 1979. The piece argues that miners correcting to oversold conditions while the underlying commodity holds above $3,900 is exactly the setup that has historically preceded sharp re-ratings for the sector.

headline: INDEPENDENCE GOLD 3TS CUTS 8.35M @ 2.39 G/T AU AND 28.98 G/T AG IN BC — Ian Vein Gold-Silver System Grows Ahead of November Follow-Up Drilling
snippet: Independence Gold (TSXV: IGO) reported additional drill results from the 3Ts Project in southern British Columbia, with hole 3TS-26-35 returning 8.35 metres grading 2.39 g/t gold and 28.98 g/t silver in the Ian vein structure. Additional holes designed to test lateral extent are planned for early November. BC's southern Interior has attracted more capital following 2024 permitting reforms, and 3Ts is building toward a maiden resource estimate on a gold-silver vein system that continues to grow with each drill campaign.
